reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a Power BI course covering business-intelligence fundamentals, Power BI concepts, and interview-question material. The course code, link, and instructor-led format indicate ordinary commercial training promotion, with no described deceptive claims, credential request, losses, or harmful condition attached to engagement.

opening.argument: The promotional path pairs a course-access action with an unusually attractive financial outcome. Viewers are directed to an external training offer using a discount code, while the presentation later supplies a salary figure of about 50,000 pounds for a three-month period and urges people to move into the field early. That combination can make purchasing or contacting the provider appear to be a low-barrier route to substantial income, even though the material does not establish that the outcome is typical, guaranteed, or independently verified.

when you look at the salary average, it's somewhere about 50,000 pounds for a three month.
So it's always helpful if you move into this field the beginning itself

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling this ordinary training does not resolve the solicitation. The title and module descriptions establish the subject matter, but they do not substantiate the financial outcome attached to entering the field. The external course link, discount code, support offer, project grade, and certificate create a concrete participation path, while the salary statement supplies the inducement. Nothing in the opening shows that the advertised economic implication is qualified or verified.

At the end of the training you will have to work on a project, based on which we will provide you a Grade and a Verifiable Certificate!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited salary discussion is not a promise that buying this course produces a payment. It describes a market figure and explicitly says the graph represents a three-month tenure, while the course material is about learning Power BI. The presence of a link and discount code shows promotion, but it does not show a guaranteed return, required deposit, or deceptive claim. The evidence therefore supports commercial education, not a linked cash-acquisition scheme.

opening.argument: Several signals become concerning when read together: an external enrollment URL, a promotional code, a certificate-oriented course funnel, and a conspicuous income figure. The presentation also lowers the perceived barrier by saying Power BI can be used by people with no technical knowledge, while describing rapidly growing opportunities. That framing can encourage viewers to treat enrollment as an easy path toward substantial earnings, even though the evidence does not provide a basis for the salary figure or establish typical results.

citations.quote: Edureka Power BI Training (Use Code: YOUTUBE20) - https://www.edureka.co/power-bi-certification-training
It can be used by people who have some technical knowledge. And also can be used by people who have no technical knowledge as well.
Now the rate of growth is somewhere about three percent every month at the current scenario.
when you look at the salary average, it's somewhere about 50,000 pounds for a three month.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats each signal in isolation. A business-intelligence topic can still be used to sell an allegedly easy economic opportunity. The cited course structure confirms a funnel involving enrollment, assignments, grading, and a certificate; it does not validate the salary or job-growth claims. The opening statement also omits the repeated low-barrier framing and the specific income figure, which are the relevant risk signals rather than the software subject itself.

citations.quote: At the end of the training you will have to work on a project, based on which we will provide you a Grade and a Verifiable Certificate!
How easy it is for anyone to use power bi is going to bring in a lot more opportunities.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are promotional and career-oriented statements, but they still do not establish a scam category. No source says that viewers will receive cash for enrolling, that earnings are guaranteed, or that money must be deposited. The material instead describes a multi-week course with assignments and project work. A salary statistic and an accessibility claim may be optimistic, yet optimism alone is not evidence of a linked reward or deceptive acquisition flow.

opening.argument: Although presented as instruction, the video functions materially as a recruitment and sales promotion for Edureka's paid training. It directs viewers to the provider with a code, advertises instructor support and a verifiable certificate, and closes with contact details. The instructional content therefore serves to build confidence in the provider before steering viewers toward participation, while career-growth and salary language gives that participation an implied financial payoff.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's description of the modules does not negate the promotional role. The video identifies the provider, supplies a discount code and direct sales contacts, describes support and certification, and encourages entry into the field. Those are participation cues, not merely neutral software instruction. The question is whether the educational framing masks an income-oriented solicitation; the opening never addresses that combination.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Commercial promotion does not automatically become a scam. The provider's contact details, support, certificate, and discount code identify an ordinary course offer, while the video spends its stated modules teaching architecture, charts, dashboards, and interview concepts. The career language does not say that enrollment guarantees income or that viewers must pay to unlock a promised cash reward. The evidence supports promotion, but not the alleged financial mechanism.
